question: Should exact descendant output incorporated into a requester-owned result count as terminal delivery even when the requester’s final outward send fails?
rationale: After the mechanical type repair, the branch still deliberately changes the product definition of delivery from outward visibility to proven internal requester consumption.

options.title: Accept requester consumption
options.body: Treat exact rendered descendant output as delivered once consumed by the requester, regardless of final channel-send success.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Delay descendant delivered credit until the requester’s composed result reaches its final target.

options.title: Defer to durable inbox
options.body: Resolve the boundary within the broader durable completion-delivery design instead of this focused accounting path.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption
recommendation.body: Treat exact rendered descendant output as delivered once consumed by the requester, regardless of final channel-send success.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across both lifecycle state and cron delivery boundaries involved in this semantic choice.
